speaker: Unknown
en: If you turn up tomorrow and say, I want to build a thousand satellites, good luck.
zh: 如果你明天来说，我要造一千颗卫星，那祝你好运。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a capstone mission to the moon we did for NASA a few years ago that was done out of here.
zh: 那是我们几年前为 NASA 做的一次登月顶点任务，就是在这里完成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Electron rocket was under $100 million and 80 people put the first rocket into orbit.
zh: Electron 火箭用不到一亿美元和 80 个人把第一枚火箭送入了轨道。

speaker: Unknown
en: These particular missions are very difficult missions.
zh: 这些特定的任务是非常困难的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like 12-year lifespan operating in nasty, nasty radiation and they're missions that just cannot fail.
zh: 它们有大约 12 年的寿命，要在非常糟糕、非常糟糕的辐射环境下运行，而且是绝对不能失败的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have 13 acres of factory around the world.
zh: 我们在全球有 13 英亩的工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is a pretty small piece of rocket land.
zh: 所以这里只是火箭园区里很小的一块。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything we haven't seen we're not allowed to see?
zh: 有什么我们没看到、也不允许看的东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Lots.
zh: 很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just saw a tiny portion.
zh: 我们刚才只看到了很小的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are here today at Rocket Lab in Long Beach with Sir Peter Beck.
zh: 我们今天来到位于长滩的 Rocket Lab,与 Sir Peter Beck 一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having us.
zh: 感谢你们来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, thanks for coming.
zh: 哦，感谢你们来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what are we going to see today?
zh: 那我们今天要看到什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we'll try and show you a little bit of Rocket Lab.
zh: 嗯，我们会尽量给你们展示一点 Rocket Lab 的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we're spread across the entire United States and Germany and New Zealand and a little bit in Australia.
zh: 你知道，我们遍布全美国、德国、新西兰，还有一点在澳大利亚。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a lot to see, but we'll show you headquarters here, a little bit of satellite manufacturing and some engine developments.
zh: 所以有很多可看的，不过我们会带你们看看这里的总部，一点卫星制造，还有一些发动机研发。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's walk through.
zh: 我们走走看吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have one of the coolest entrances I've seen.
zh: 你这里的入口是我见过最酷的入口之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So does it remind you of anything?
zh: 那它有没有让你想起什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is how I test how much of a sci-fi nerd you are.
zh: 这是我测试你是不是科幻迷的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Star Trek?
zh: 《星际迷航》?

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's probably a little bit old.
zh: 它可能有点老了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's 2001 Space Odyssey.
zh: 是《2001 太空漫游》。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, that's exactly what I was getting at.
zh: 哦，那正是我想说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best sci-fi movie ever made because it's the most accurate.
zh: 史上最好的科幻电影，因为它是最准确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this bit is supposed to remind you of the bit where they shut down the HAL 9000 computer, you know?
zh: 而这一段应该是让你想起他们关掉 HAL 9000 计算机的那一幕，你知道吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't do that, Dave.
zh: 别这么做，Dave。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's like that.
zh: 就像那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have any other inspiration of sci-fi movies in here?
zh: 你在这里还有其他受科幻电影启发的地方吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: No?
zh: 没有？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just the one.
zh: 就这一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, when we walked in here earlier, we were kind of stuck to the timeline because it's jam-packed with so much stuff.
zh: 嗯，我们刚才走进这里的时候，基本上被这条时间线黏住了，因为上面塞满了太多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much going on.
zh: 有太多内容了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it might be cool to walk through some of that and kind of show what you have in the lobby area.
zh: 所以走一遍这些内容、展示一下你们门厅区域的东西可能会很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like a showcase.
zh: 这看起来像一个展示区。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well, like any company, it's like the 20-year overnight success.
zh: 是的，嗯，和任何公司一样，这就是那种“20 年的一夜成名”。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I started the company in 2006 down in New Zealand.
zh: 所以我在 2006 年于新西兰创办了这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sort of between 2006 and 2009, we were like our own little technology development house.
zh: 大概在 2006 到 2009 年之间，我们就像一个自己的小型技术开发屋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in 2009, we launched our first suborbital rocket called Artea-1, and we were the first private company in the southern hemisphere to reach space.
zh: 2009 年，我们发射了第一枚亚轨道火箭，叫 Artea-1,我们是南半球第一家到达太空的私营公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not orbit, just into space.
zh: 不是轨道，只是进入了太空。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just three years after starting.
zh: 就在创立之后短短三年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yep.
zh: 是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with like 80, I think we had a total capitalization of under 100,000 New Zealand dollars, which is like 60,000 US dollars at that point.
zh: 而且我记得我们当时的总资本还不到十万新西兰元，大概相当于那时候的六万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to think there's billionaires starting companies now that don't actually reach space.
zh: 想想现在有些亿万富翁创办公司，却根本到不了太空。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is true, yeah.
zh: 确实如此，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think one of the success stories of Rocket Lab has been, we have this saying, well, it's actually, we stole it from Ernest Rutherford, and that's why the engine is called Rutherford.
zh: 我是说，我觉得 Rocket Lab 的成功故事之一就是，我们有这么一句话——其实这话是我们从 Ernest Rutherford 那里偷来的，所以那台发动机才叫 Rutherford。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, we have no money, so we have to think.
zh: 他说过：我们没有钱，所以我们得动脑子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's kind of the ethos of the company.
zh: 这差不多就是这家公司的精神。

speaker: Unknown
en: We came from very humble beginnings.
zh: 我们起点非常寒微。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on that rocket actually is like a swage lock fittings that I'd salvaged from a junkyard.
zh: 而且那枚火箭上用的那些 swage lock 接头，实际上是我从废品场里捡来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, yeah, because I could only afford the ferrules, not the cost of the fittings.
zh: 是啊，因为我只买得起套管，买不起整套接头。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would get the fitting from the junkyard and buy the $3.20 ferrules to put in it and recondition it into a fitting.
zh: 所以我就从废品场弄来接头，然后买三块二的套管装上去，把它翻新成一个接头。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was seriously constrained stuff.
zh: 所以那真是物资极度匮乏的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: From that adversity comes good ideas.
zh: 从那种逆境中会产生好点子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then in 2010, we won some work with DARPA and developed a new kind of propellant and propulsion system, did a little instantizer rocket launch UAV.
zh: 然后在 2010 年，我们拿到了 DARPA 的一些项目，开发了一种新型推进剂和推进系统，还做了一个小型即时火箭发射 UAV。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then 2013 is really where we started to grow up.
zh: 然后 2013 年才是我们真正开始成长的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's when I went out of New Zealand and came here to the United States and started raising our first venture capital.
zh: 那年我离开新西兰，来到美国，开始募集我们的第一笔风险投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Kozla Ventures were the first folks to put in some venture capital into the entity.
zh: Kozla Ventures 是第一个向这家实体注入风险资本的机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at that point, we flipped from being a New Zealand company into a US company.
zh: 到那时，我们从一家新西兰公司转变成了美国公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Kozla put $5 million in for the Series A round, which, you know, at that time for me, that was the most insane amount of money imaginable.
zh: Kozla 在 A 轮投了五百万美元，你知道，对我而言，在当时那简直是能想象到的最不可思议的一笔巨款。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for that, you know, we got our first 3D printed Rutherford engine hot fired and proved out a whole lot of composite structures and stuff.
zh: 但凭借这笔钱，我们完成了第一台 3D 打印 Rutherford 发动机的点火试车，并验证了大量复合材料结构之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ended the B round in 2014 with Bessemer leading that.
zh: 2014 年结束了 B 轮，由 Bessemer 领投。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then 2015 we broke ground on our Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand, so that was the very first private orbital launch site.
zh: 然后 2015 年我们在新西兰动工修建了 Launch Complex 1，那是第一个私人轨道发射场。

speaker: Unknown
en: 2016 we finished it.
zh: 2016 年我们建成了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: 2017 we launched our first vehicle and we raised our D round, which became a unicorn at that point.
zh: 2017 年我们发射了第一枚火箭，并募集了 D 轮，在那时成为了独角兽。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's when...
zh: 那时候……

speaker: Unknown
en: Big deal.
zh: 了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things started to move a bit, yeah.
zh: 事情开始有起色了，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, 2018, we launched three rockets, and probably the fourth rocket in the stable there, number four, was one of the, I guess for me personally, one of the more satisfying ones, because...
zh: 然后，2018 年，我们发射了三枚火箭，而机库里大概的第四枚火箭，也就是第四枚，对我个人来说，是更令人满足的一枚，因为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Prior to this, I was a kid sitting in New Zealand dreaming working for NASA.
zh: 在那之前，我只是个坐在新西兰梦想着为 NASA 工作的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had this little plastic space shuttle that would sit in my desk beside me.
zh: 我有一个小小的塑料航天飞机模型，就摆在我桌边。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when I started my career in engineering, it used to sit on the top of my toolbox and then the top of my laptop and so on and so forth.
zh: 后来我开始工程师生涯时，它就放在我工具箱顶上，然后是笔记本电脑顶上，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I never really got to be employed by NASA, but I got to launch their payloads.
zh: 我从来没有真正被 NASA 雇用过，但我发射了他们的载荷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you couldn't be employed by NASA because you didn't go to college, right?
zh: 而你进不了 NASA 是因为你没上过大学，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, no, I was objectively too dumb.
zh: 是啊，没错，客观上讲我太笨了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also a foreign national, so foreign national, no degree, you know, it wasn't looking good.
zh: 而且还是外国公民，所以外国公民、没有学位，你知道，前景不妙。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does that bleed into the culture here?
zh: 那这些是怎么融入这里的文化的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I've heard that you're a wire eight type of person.
zh: 我听说你是“八号线材”类型的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is that?
zh: 那是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, no, it's a New Zealand saying, number eight wire.
zh: 哦，不，那是句新西兰俗语，“八号线材”。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually personally hate it.
zh: 我个人其实很讨厌它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it means, well, it's got two connotations.
zh: 因为它的意思是——嗯，它有两层含义。

speaker: Unknown
en: In New Zealand, it means to, you know, to bodge stuff together.
zh: 在新西兰，它指的是把东西胡乱凑合到一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm the opposite of a bodge stuff together kind of guy.
zh: 而我恰恰是那种凑合派的反面。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's kind of subliminal meaning is more making do with not much, which I think is technically accurate.
zh: 但它更隐含的意思是用手头不多的东西将就着办，我觉得从技术上讲这倒是准确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how does that, even from the beginning, how does that bleed into the culture today?
zh: 那么从最开始，这些是如何融入今天的文化的呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, today, if you look at what we achieve with the amount of capital resources that we expend, it's always pretty significantly better than most people.
zh: 嗯,今天,如果你看看我们用所花费的资本资源所取得的成就,总是比大多数人要好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, the Electron rocket, I think it was under $100 million and 80 people put the first rocket into orbit.
zh: 举例来说,Electron 火箭,我认为是花了不到 1 亿美元、80 个人就把第一枚火箭送入了轨道。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the time, our nearest competitor was Virgin Orbit, and that was funded by Sir Richard Branson.
zh: 当时,离我们最近的竞争对手是 Virgin Orbit,它由 Sir Richard Branson 资助。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the end, I think Richard put $1.2 billion into that company before it ultimately went bankrupt with a handful of launches under their belt.
zh: 到最后,我认为 Richard 在那家公司破产之前投入了 12 亿美元,而它只完成了寥寥几次发射。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, we are never the most well financed, although as a public company, we're certainly much more endowed than we ever have been.
zh: 所以是的,我们从来都不是资金最雄厚的,尽管作为一家上市公司,我们肯定比以往任何时候都要充裕得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I mean, it's sort of hard baked into the culture here that everything is ground right down to the very last bit.
zh: 但我的意思是,把一切都精打细算到最后一分钱,这已经深深烙印在我们的文化里了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was an interview we did where someone mentioned that startups often die from indigestion of funding.
zh: 我们做过一次访谈,有人提到创业公司常常死于“资金消化不良”。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at, if I look back and think of, you know, lots of startups that I've seen or been involved with, the ones that have failed most spectacularly have been the ones that have been funded the most well, you know, the most significantly.
zh: 如果你看看——如果我回顾一下,你知道,我见过的或参与过的很多创业公司,失败得最惨烈的,恰恰是那些融资最充足、你知道,融资规模最大的那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is brought to you by Brex, my favorite.
zh: 本期节目由 Brex 呈现,我的最爱。

speaker: Unknown
en: You become what you spend on, and I refuse to spend my time on work that shouldn't exist.
zh: 你会变成你所消费的东西,而我拒绝把时间花在不该存在的工作上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Expense reports, receipt chasing, and manual closes.
zh: 报销单、追讨收据和手动结账。

speaker: Unknown
en: The companies building what's next from Vercel, OpenAI, Anthropic, Granola, and Deepgram all made the same call.
zh: 那些正在构建未来的公司——从 Vercel、OpenAI、Anthropic、Granola 到 Deepgram——都做出了同样的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all run on Brex.
zh: 它们都在用 Brex。

speaker: Unknown
en: Brex is the intelligent finance platform that combines cards, expenses, and banking into a single stack.
zh: Brex 是一个智能金融平台,将卡、支出和银行业务整合到一个体系中。

speaker: Unknown
en: With agentic finance built in.
zh: 内置智能体金融。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI agents that handle expenses automatically, enforce policy before spend happens, and close your books in minutes.
zh: AI 智能体可以自动处理报销、在支出发生前执行政策,并在几分钟内结清账目。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why Sorcery runs on Brex, so I can spend time on building and not busy work.
zh: 这就是为什么 Sorcery 用 Brex,这样我就可以把时间花在构建上,而不是琐碎事务上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's time to get Brex AF.
zh: 是时候 Brex AF 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at brex.com slash sorcery.
zh: 访问 brex.com/sorcery 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's B-R-E-X dot com slash S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y.
zh: 也就是 B-R-E-X dot com slash S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bye.
zh: 再见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turing is training the next generation of AI with tasks that require real expertise and real-world judgment.
zh: Turing 正在用需要真正专业知识和真实世界判断力的任务来训练下一代 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why companies like NVIDIA, Anthropic, Salesforce, and Gemini partner with Turing.
zh: 这就是为什么 NVIDIA、Anthropic、Salesforce 和 Gemini 等公司与 Turing 合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turing builds realistic reinforcement learning environments and data systems based on real operational traces, the kind of infrastructure Frontier Labs need to train superintelligence.
zh: Turing 基于真实运营痕迹构建逼真的强化学习环境和数据系统,正是 Frontier Labs 训练超级智能所需的那类基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit Turing.com slash S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y.
zh: 访问 Turing.com/S-O-U-R-C-E-R-Y。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as we walk through the timeline, there's a really interesting point where you just 2021, you go public and you make a ton of acquisitions.
zh: 那么当我们梳理这条时间线时,有一个非常有趣的节点,就是 2021 年,你上市并进行了大量收购。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what kind of was the process for going public here?
zh: 那么当时上市的过程是怎样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do you see that happening to today with everything that's going on with SpaceX?
zh: 而结合现在 SpaceX 正在发生的一切,你如何看待今天上市的走势?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so there was a couple of reasons to go public.
zh: 是的,上市有几个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: One kind of logically and one kind of almost, well sort of logically, but personal.
zh: 一个算得上合乎逻辑的,另一个几乎……算是一半合乎逻辑,一半是个人原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think being a public company teaches you extreme discipline.
zh: 我认为成为一家上市公司会让你学会极度的纪律性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you can't be messing around as a public company and wasting capital and not delivering.
zh: 作为上市公司,你不能胡来、浪费资本、不交付成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the company has always had a really strong culture of delivery, but as a public company, it's just even much, much more intense.
zh: 所以公司一直有着非常强的交付文化,但作为上市公司,这种强度要高得多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then sort of the personal reason why I wanted to take the company public is I'm trying to build a multi-generational space company.
zh: 而我想让公司上市的个人原因是,我正在努力打造一家跨越数代人的航天公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so many companies in this industry are defined by their founders or a small group of people.
zh: 这个行业里太多的公司是由它们的创始人或一小群人来定义的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have to ask yourself when they ultimately kick the bucket, what happens to those companies?
zh: 你必须扪心自问,当他们最终咽气之后,这些公司会怎样?

speaker: Unknown
en: And the only thing that my parents ever said to me as I was growing up was, have impact.
zh: 而在我成长过程中,我父母对我说的唯一一句话就是:要有影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have the most amount of impact in your lifetime.
zh: 在你的一生中产生最大的影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can have, you know, amount of impact when you're alive, but if you can, you know, keep that impact going after you're dead, then you, you know, by proxy, you have much, much larger impact.
zh: 所以你可以在,你知道,在世时产生一定的影响力,但如果你能让这种影响力在你死后延续下去,那么你,你知道,通过代理,你就拥有了更大的影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the idea here with going public is enforcing that discipline so that when I'm long gone, this thing just keeps going and going and going and going.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
